newsitem.title: LATVIA: PRIVATE PENSION FUND LAW PASSED.
newsitem.headline: PRIVATE PENSION FUND LAW PASSED.

text.p: Parliament has passed a private pension fund law which will be effective from the start of next year, the labour and social issues committee said on Friday.
"The law is effective from January 1, 1998 and will regulate the functioning of private pension funds as non-profit finance and credit institutions," a committee spokeswoman told Reuters.
The funds, which provide the possibility of saving in aaddition to the state pension sheme, will be supervised by the state insurance inspection.

The right to operate a fund will be limited to licensed banks, life insurance companies and brokerages or investment companies. The rule applies to banks with licences for securities transactions and accepting individual deposits.
The committee also said that following the passing of the investment companies law, expected next year, only banks and insurance companies will have the right to run a pension fund.
